title: General Tso’s Garlic-Chile Sauce
description: A dark, glossy Chinese-American takeout sauce balances toasted mild chile, fresh ginger and a small, sharp splash of rice vinegar.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: ground ancho chile
ingredients.note: Use pure mild ancho, without added salt.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

steps.title: Bloom the chile
steps.text: Warm {oil} in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Stir in {ga} and {an} for 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Build the glaze
steps.text: Whisk in {gi}, {ch}, {a}, {bs}, {rv} and {to}. Simmer uncovered for 4 minutes until the sugar dissolves and the color deepens.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon the warm sauce over moist chicken thighs or steamed cauliflower. Pass extra ground chile at the table.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 5 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the vinegar and omit the ancho. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 58 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 11.3 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 124 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 53 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 10.0 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.4 g fiber, 34 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
